passages.observation: Israel is invited to bring materials so that God may dwell among them according to the shown pattern.

passages.title: The land keeps Sabbath and cannot be sold forever

passages.observation: The land rests, liberty is proclaimed, property returns, and God names the land as his while Israel are tenants and foreigners.

passages.title: Obedience is pictured as secure dwelling

passages.observation: Rain, harvest, peace, divine dwelling, and upright walking are joined to covenant faithfulness.

passages.title: Scattering is threatened and covenant is remembered

passages.observation: Israel is commanded to love the LORD and teach the words when entering cities, houses, wells, and vineyards they did not build.

passages.observation: The promised land differs from Egypt, receives rain, and may lose rain if Israel turns to other gods.

passages.title: Blessing fills city, field, and dwelling

passages.observation: Obedience is described through fertility, provision, victory, rain, lending, and being established as a holy people.

passages.title: Curse ends in siege, scattering, and return to Egypt

passages.observation: Disobedience reverses blessing through disease, failed harvest, siege, exile among nations, and a final journey back toward bondage.

passages.title: A devastated land becomes a question for later generations

passages.title: Return from the nations is promised after return to God

passages.observation: When blessing and curse are remembered among the nations, God gathers, restores, circumcises the heart, and renews abundance.

passages.title: Life and death are set before the people

passages.title: Israel receives land, rest, and fulfilled promise

passages.title: Israel crosses the Jordan on dry ground

passages.title: Joshua warns that covenant breach can remove Israel

passages.title: A generation forgets and the land becomes pressure

passages.title: Solomon asks heaven to hear toward the temple

passages.title: Prayer anticipates captivity in an enemy land

passages.title: Temple and land are made conditional signs

passages.observation: God consecrates the house yet warns that turning away will cut Israel from the land and make the temple a public astonishment.

passages.title: Solomon’s turned heart fractures the kingdom

passages.title: Israel is carried to Assyria

passages.title: Jerusalem and the temple are destroyed

passages.observation: Siege, famine, capture, execution, burning, broken walls, removed vessels, and deportation bring Judah’s kingdom to collapse.

passages.title: Healing the land stands beside possible uprooting

passages.title: Exile, land Sabbath, and Cyrus close Chronicles

passages.title: Cyrus authorizes return and rebuilding
